newsitem.title: CANADA: Several Canada oil stocks hit by share price drops.
newsitem.headline: Several Canada oil stocks hit by share price drops.

text.p: Several large Canadian oil and gas firms experienced big stock price slides on Tuesday amid increasing uncertainty over energy market conditions, analysts said.

Big losers in today's Toronto Stock Exchange session included Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, down 1.50 to 33.50, Alberta Energy Co Ltd down 1 to 32.50, Imperial Oil Ltd down 0.85 to 69.95 and Talisman Energy Inc down 0.65 to 41.85.
"I think it's a correction, but I don't think it's the end of the market by any means," said Ken Faircloth, analyst with Goepel Shields & Partners.

Faircloth said he expected oil prices, which have fallen by almost US$3 a barrel since their May highs, to come under further pressure as the summer wore on, a situation likely to extend to the oil stock market.

Another factor affecting Canadian oils was the widening differential between heavy oil -- a fast-growing crude grade for numerous companies such as like CanOxy and Canadian Natural Resources Ltd -- and light crude in refining markets, said John S. Herold Inc analyst Bob Gillon.
Canadian Natural fell 0.55 to 35 in Toronto today.
The TSE Oil & Gas sub-index, which rose to an all-time high of 7,161 points in late May, has since shed six percent to close at 6,720 on Tuesday, down 64.48 points on the day.
"There's some (downward) momentum. People are laying off a little bit of stock here," Faircloth said.

"It started with Renaissance last week and people are translating that into thinking there will be further problems, even though they are not totally identified. And I'm not sure whether that will be the case or not."
Renaissance Energy Ltd shocked the market last week with news that it did not expect to meet its oil production forecasts this year.
The broad TSE 300 Composite Index, meanwhile, closed up 16.3 points to a record 6655.9 today.
